subject: Urgent: Aurora Biosystems VPC - intermittent 500s and tokenization latency
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@aurorabio.com>

Cc: Luke Price <luke.price@aurorabio.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Apr 2026 16:12:00 +0100
Subject: Re: production errors in VPC this morning

Hi Lauren,

We started seeing a spike of 500s and large per-request tokenization latency on our private VPC cluster this morning (~08:30 UTC). The errors are intermittent but impacting batch processing for our nightly ingestion pipeline — throughput has dropped by ~45% and several jobs timed out. We've attached a short sample of the error logs and a trace of a slow request.

Can you confirm whether any recent rollout or kernel change could be causing this? Our execs are already asking for an RCA.

Attachments: error-sample-logs.txt (text), slow-request-trace.json (referenced inline)

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Engineering
Aurora Biosystems

Quick asks for your team to help us triage faster:
- Can you confirm whether you observed any config pushes or model swaps in the last 24 hours?

I’ll keep you updated in this thread.

— Lauren Bishop

From: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@aurorabio.com>
Cc: hiro_tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 26 Apr 2026 09:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: production errors in VPC this morning

Thanks Samira — I pulled the attached log sample and ran a quick grep for 5xx and tokenization warnings. Initial findings: 
- There are repeated "KV cache miss" entries followed by long tail latencies for tokenization (~700-1,200ms) on requests that should be hitting cache.
- Error 502/503 are originating from the inference runtime process (nginx is healthy).
- No model swap recorded in our control-plane activity logs for Aurora between 2026-04-24 00:00 UTC and 2026-04-25 12:00 UTC.

Next steps we’re executing now:
1) Collect a kernel-level perf trace from the affected node (requesting elevated logs from your team; please keep the pod alive).
2) Push a lightweight hotfix to disable a recent experimental kv-cache eviction policy on your private runtime (non-disruptive restart path).
3) If that doesn’t improve, we’ll failover a percentage of traffic to our fallback hosted routing for the critical ingestion job (requires approval).

I’ve attached an initial profiling snapshot we generated after replaying the trace — see profiling-report-aurora-2026-04-27.pdf (will follow with a full perf trace).

— Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
Attachments: profiling-report-aurora-2026-04-27.pdf (pdf)
From: hiro_tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@aurorabio.com>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Apr 2026 10:12:00 +0100
Subject: Re: production errors in VPC this morning

Following up on Dev’s notes — I dug into the perf trace and there are two converging issues:
- Tokenizer subprocess occasionally blocks on shared-file locks when multiple long sequences are tokenized concurrently. This shows up as ~500-1,200ms tokenization latency spikes.
- Our adaptive batching heuristics combined with a configuration mismatch on the customer autoscaler produced batch sizes that exceeded the current KV cache slot allocation, causing cache churn and transient 502s.

Immediate mitigations we recommend (non-disruptive where possible):
- Disable tokenizer parallelism at the process level for your runtime config (config flag: tokenizer.parallel=false). This reduces max tokenization latency at the cost of a small CPU increase.
- Reduce max_batch_size on the served route from 64 -> 32 for the ingestion job for the next 12 hours while we monitor.

I can push the tokenizer change as a live config update; reducing batch size requires a planned restart window from your ops team. Please confirm window availability.

— Hiro Tanaka
On-call Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Luke Price <luke.price@aurorabio.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@aurorabio.com>
Cc: Jason Meyers <j.meyers@aurorabio.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Apr 2026 14:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: production errors in VPC this morning

Lauren — appreciate the rapid attention. Our CTO and CISO are briefing execs now; they’ve asked for a mitigation timeline and whether this counts as an SLA incident (we have a monthly uptime commitment tied to batch throughput).

We need two things:
1) A guaranteed short-term mitigation by EOD tomorrow that prevents ingestion job timeouts (if routing to hosted fallback is necessary, confirm data residency implications).
2) A written plan for the next 72 hours and a scheduled exec update (30 min) to be booked with Aurora leadership.

I’m attaching the message our operations lead prepared for internal stakeholders (PDF forwarded).

— Luke Price
VP, Engineering — Aurora Biosystems
From: evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: production errors in VPC this morning

Luke / Aurora team — thanks for outlining the ask. Quick executive note and next steps from our side:
- Short-term mitigation: We will disable tokenizer.parallel on your runtime today (non-disruptive hot config) and request a restart window for batch size reduction tonight 22:00-23:00 CEST. If your ops cannot do 22:00, propose the nearest 2-hour window and we’ll accommodate.
- If the restart window is not feasible, we will temporarily route the ingestion job to our hosted fallback for a maximum of 6 hours; this requires a signed data residency exception form (link below).
- We’re scheduling a 30-minute exec sync for Wed 2026-04-29 09:00 CEST — please confirm attendees. Lauren and I will attend from Redwood. Dev and Hiro will provide the technical runbook and postmortem within 48 hours.

Action items for Aurora ops:
- Confirm restart window for batch size change.
- If routing to hosted fallback is acceptable, sign the data residency exception form: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AuroraRunbook

We will update the incident ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/INC-2026-7831

— Evelyn Hart
